messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: service=\"inference-queue\" severity=P1 — queue depth exceeded threshold (50,412). page fired to rotation. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-98123

pagerduty: Incident PD-98123 created and routed to ENG-ONCALL. Escalation policy: oncall -> sre -> eng-lead. Trigger: queue_backlog_high.

Alex R.: acked. oncall taking. starting triage — first check autoscaler and queue consumer lag.

Maria C.: saw spike ~5m ago in producer traffic (ingest pipeline). Could be sudden batch job. Can we see which tenant or path?

Jamal S.: checking consumer lag and node utilization. running quick queries:

sre-bot: ```
# k8s HPA status
kubectl -n inference get hpa inference-consumer -o wide
# prometheus: queue depth
promql: sum(queue_length{queue=\"inference\"})
```

Jamal S.: HPA target=5 pods, current replicas=5, cpu avg=92%, gpu-util ~98% on pods. queue length per pod ~10k. Autoscaler didn't kick due to maxReplicas=5.

Priya K.: confirmed — autoscaler hit upper limit. We have reserved-gpu-pool max=5. Need either quick capacity increase or shed non-critical work.

Alex R.: option A: temporarily raise maxReplicas and increase node pool; option B: enable degraded mode (throttle low-priority tenants) and flush backlog; option C: failover to smaller model to reduce per-token latency. Thoughts?

Maria C.: can we rate-limit ingestion for background sync jobs? I can flip a flag in the ingestion service. That should quickly reduce pressure while we scale.

Jamal S.: I'll attempt to increase node pool manually in GCP. command: ```gcloud container clusters resize inference-cluster --node-pool=gpu-pool --num-nodes=10 --zone=us-central1-a``` This will add nodes; but provisioning ~3-5m.

Alex R.: do it. also open a request to infra to temporarily lift maxReplicas to 10 for HPA. Maria, Priya — can you coordinate throttles?

Maria C.: flipping ingestion flag now -> `POST /admin/feature/ingest-rate-limit` payload {\"rate\": \"20/s\"} — rolling. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: ingestion-rate-limit: success. producers now throttled to 20/s for background-sync.

Jamal S.: started resize. `operation-12345` kicked off. estimated node ready ~4m.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded: Alex R. (on-call) acknowledged the page at 1765039135.

Priya K.: also enabling request prioritization in the router to favor interactive traffic. patch: ```
# envoy config patch
priority: high -> interactive
rate_limit: background 10r/s
``` Applying now.

Alex R.: good. Once nodes ready, I'll bump HPA maxReplicas to 10:
```kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-consumer -p '{\"spec\":{\"maxReplicas\":10}}'```

Jamal S.: nodes are coming up. current node count = 7 (added 2). pods pending scheduling on GPUs — kube-scheduler backlog short.

sre-bot: autoscaler note: cluster autoscaler scaling activity: ScaleUp in progress (2 nodes).

Maria C.: seeing queue ingestion drop by ~40% after throttle. interactive latency still high for a subset — some requests are stuck in long queue.

Alex R.: done: patched HPA maxReplicas to 10 and increased deployment minReadySeconds to speed up rollout. Applying: `kubectl apply -f deployment/consumer-scaling.yml`

Jamal S.: HPA now showing desiredReplicas=9, current=6 -> scaling up pods. GPU scheduling delays minimal.

Priya K.: router prioritization effective — 95th latency for interactive dropped from 2.2s -> 720ms for new requests.

pagerduty: Incident PD-98123 status: acknowledged -> in_progress.

Alex R.: marking customer impact: degraded throughput for all tenants, visible error 429 for a small percentage of background jobs, interactive degradation for ~15% of requests. Current mitigation: ingestion throttled, HPA and node pool increased. ETA for full catch-up ~10-15m.

Jamal S.: queue depth trending down: now 23,400 (was 50,412). consumer pod CPU ~70%, GPU ~80%. Continuing to scale until steady.

Maria C.: I pushed a temporary config to move low-priority tenants to fallback model (smaller) which reduces per-request GPU time by ~50%. Should help drain backlog as well.

Alex R.: good. Can we confirm no customer-facing errors beyond transient latency?

Priya K.: checking logs -> only background sync shows 429/503 spikes. No 5xx for interactive endpoints in the last 10m.

pagerduty: Escalation suppressed: oncall handling. No rotation escalation needed.

Jamal S.: scaling stabilized at 9 pods, queue now ~6,800. Node pool at desired 9 nodes.

Alex R.: marking incident as mitigated in-progress. We should keep monitoring for 30m. I'll add postmortem owners.

Maria C.: action items: (1) remove ingestion throttle after backlog drained, (2) revert fallback-model routing, (3) review autoscaler limits and set a higher safety margin for peak windows.

Priya K.: I'll open a ticket and schedule an ops-runbook update.

sre-bot: Incident PD-98123: mitigation started at 1765039135, current status: recovering.

Alex R.: thanks everyone. handing off monitoring to SRE second-shift (Jamal will stay on for 10m then hand to SRE).

Jamal S.: noted. I’ll stay for 10m and then pass to oncall-next.

pagerduty: Incident PD-98123 updated: status=resolved? No — still open. Will auto-resolve when backlog < 1000 for 15m.

Alex R.: final: backlog under 7k and falling. closing thread here; we'll draft postmortem with timeline and follow-ups. :memo:
